title: Fiction
blurb: Novels and stories — the truth told through invention.

planned.title: Don Quixote
planned.author: Miguel de Cervantes
planned.note: The first modern novel, entire — a mad knight, his earthbound squire, and the comedy of ideals meeting the world.

planned.title: One Thousand and One Nights
planned.note: Scheherazade's treasury of tales — the wellspring of the frame narrative.

planned.title: The Tale of Genji
planned.author: Murasaki Shikibu
planned.note: The world's first psychological novel — the loves and aging of a Heian prince, written by a woman a thousand years ago.

planned.title: Candide
planned.author: Voltaire
planned.note: Voltaire's lightning satire — innocence loose in a brutal world, and the case for tending one's garden.

planned.title: Pride and Prejudice
planned.author: Jane Austen
planned.note: Austen's perfect comedy of manners — wit, money, and the slow education of the heart.

planned.title: The Brothers Karamazov
planned.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
planned.note: Dostoevsky's final novel — a murder, three brothers, and the deepest argument in fiction over God and freedom.

planned.title: Frankenstein
planned.author: Mary Shelley
planned.note: A teenager invents science fiction — the creature, its maker, and the terror of what we make.

planned.title: Gargantua and Pantagruel
planned.author: François Rabelais
planned.note: Rabelais's giant, riotous satire — learning and appetite, the body and the book, in full Renaissance laughter.

planned.title: Gulliver's Travels
planned.author: Jonathan Swift
planned.note: Swift's voyages to impossible lands — the sharpest satire of human folly ever written.

planned.title: Moby-Dick
planned.author: Herman Melville
planned.note: Melville's white whale — an American epic of obsession, the sea, and the unknowable.

planned.title: Great Expectations
planned.author: Charles Dickens
planned.note: Dickens's masterpiece of self-deception — a poor boy, a secret fortune, and the cost of becoming a gentleman.

planned.title: War and Peace
planned.author: Leo Tolstoy
planned.note: Tolstoy's vast novel of Russia at war with Napoleon — the whole of life held in one book.

planned.title: Middlemarch
planned.author: George Eliot
planned.note: George Eliot's study of a provincial town — the grandest English novel of ordinary lives and thwarted hopes.

planned.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
planned.author: Mark Twain
planned.note: Twain's runaway boy and a freedom-seeking man on a raft — the great American novel of conscience.

planned.title: Heart of Darkness
planned.author: Joseph Conrad
planned.note: Conrad's voyage up the Congo into the heart of empire — and of human darkness.

planned.title: Ulysses
planned.author: James Joyce
planned.note: Joyce remakes the novel — one Dublin day rendered whole, the Odyssey turned inside out.

planned.title: The Trial
planned.author: Franz Kafka
planned.note: Kafka's nightmare of a man arrested for a crime never named — the modern condition as parable.

planned.title: The Panchatantra
planned.author: Anonymous
planned.note: The world's most-traveled fables — animal tales of cunning and rule that reached every continent.

planned.title: Romance of the Three Kingdoms
planned.author: Luo Guanzhong
planned.note: China's great historical epic — war, loyalty, and strategy in the empire's collapse.

planned.title: The Water Margin
planned.author: Shi Nai'an
planned.note: Outlaws of the marsh — a band of rebels turned folk heroes, China's tale of honor among bandits.

planned.title: Journey to the West
planned.author: Wu Cheng'en
planned.note: The Monkey King escorts a monk to fetch the scriptures — China's beloved comic-spiritual epic.

planned.title: Dream of the Red Chamber
planned.author: Cao Xueqin
planned.note: The slow ruin of a great family seen through a doomed love — the subtlest of the Chinese novels.

planned.title: The Maqamat
planned.author: Al-Hariri
planned.note: Al-Hariri's dazzling tales of a silver-tongued rogue — the showpiece of classical Arabic prose.

planned.title: The Decameron
planned.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
planned.note: A hundred tales told by ten young Florentines fleeing the plague — the birth of European prose fiction.

planned.title: Robinson Crusoe
planned.author: Daniel Defoe
planned.note: The castaway who built a world from nothing — often called the first English novel.

planned.title: The Red and the Black
planned.author: Stendhal
planned.note: A carpenter's son claws toward the top of Restoration France — the first great psychological novel.

planned.title: Madame Bovary
planned.author: Gustave Flaubert
planned.note: A provincial wife dreams beyond her life — the novel that made prose an exact art.

planned.title: Les Misérables
planned.author: Victor Hugo
planned.note: An ex-convict's long redemption against the barricades of Paris — the great novel of mercy and justice.

planned.title: Jane Eyre
planned.author: Charlotte Brontë
planned.note: A governess who will not be owned — the novel that gave the heroine her own fierce voice.

planned.title: Wuthering Heights
planned.author: Emily Brontë
planned.note: Love as a force of nature on the Yorkshire moors — wild, strange, and unlike anything before it.

planned.title: In Search of Lost Time
planned.author: Marcel Proust
planned.note: Memory, time, and a taste of cake — the longest and deepest novel of the modern age.

planned.title: Mrs Dalloway
planned.author: Virginia Woolf
planned.note: One London day inside many minds — Woolf remakes the novel as the flow of consciousness.

planned.title: The Stranger
planned.author: Albert Camus
planned.note: A man who feels nothing at his mother's funeral — the novel of the absurd that defined an era.

planned.author: George Orwell
planned.note: Big Brother, Newspeak, and the boot on the human face forever — the century's defining dystopia.

planned.title: The Old Man and the Sea
planned.author: Ernest Hemingway
planned.note: An old fisherman, a great marlin, and the dignity of struggle — Hemingway at his sparest.

planned.title: Things Fall Apart
planned.author: Chinua Achebe
planned.note: An Igbo leader and the coming of the British — the novel that gave modern African literature its voice.

planned.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
planned.author: Gabriel García Márquez
planned.note: The Buendía family across generations — the masterpiece of magical realism.

planned.title: Beloved
planned.author: Toni Morrison
planned.note: A mother, a ghost, and the unhealed wound of slavery — the great American novel of memory.

planned.title: The Pilgrim's Progress
planned.author: John Bunyan
planned.note: The great allegory of the Christian life as a perilous journey.

planned.title: Folklore and Fable
planned.author: Aesop, Grimm & Andersen
planned.note: Aesop, Grimm, and Andersen — the fables and fairy tales that raised the West.

planned.title: The Betrothed
planned.author: Alessandro Manzoni
planned.note: Italy's great historical novel — two lovers kept apart by power and plague.
